newsitem.title: USA: Exploration delineation well finds natgas.
newsitem.headline: Exploration delineation well finds natgas.

text.p: Exploration Co said Tuesday it has tested natural gas from its Paloma "C" No. 2-108 in the Glen Rose formation in Maverick County, Texas.
The well flowed 340,000 cubic feet per day with production of one barrel of condensate per day and 23 barrels of water per day through perforations from 5,597 to 5,600 feet.
This well is about half a mile west of the Paloma No. 1-107 which had an open flow of 44 million cubic feet per day from a separate reef, said President James E. Sigmon.
About 130 feet of reef was encountered but only the top 10 feet appears to contain natural gas.

"We intend to keep the production rate of this well relatively low in order to reduce the possibility of increasing the water production. Every well drilled in this zone enhances our geologic model giving us more confidence in the outcome of drilling using our 3-D seismic to locate these potentially prolific patch reefs," Sigmon said.
Exploration Co owns a 55 percent working interest in the Paloma "C" No. 2-108 but has at least a 60 percent interest in the remaining 50,000 acres in its leasehold.
Sigmon also said the company plans to begin drilling another test on the Maverick County leasehold in March.
